candana.notes: MN 133 has an unnamed deity visiting Samiddhi. The named visitor to Lomasakaṅgiya is in MN 134. SN 2.14, 2.16, 2.17 and 40.10 feature Nandana, Vāsudatta, Subrahmā and Sakka respectively.

candanaṅgalika.notes: The lay follower receives the five robes in SN 3.12. SN 3.13 concerns Pasenadi’s eating. The Aṅguttara citation compares a different speaker, the brahmin Piṅgīyānī, who recites the verse in AN 5.195. AN 5.194 is the preceding discourse.

caṅkī.notes: The entry’s reference to the gathering at Icchānaṅgala can be placed at Snp 3.9:1.4, with a parallel at MN 98:2.2.

caṇḍa.notes: The packet misses SN 42.1:1.2 and 3.1. Both explicitly name caṇḍo gāmaṇi, which Sujato translates as ‘Fury the chief’. The intervening discussion also uses caṇḍa as an adjective.

chaddanta.notes: AN 7.66:6.2–3 lists Chaddantā among the lakes from which rivers flow. The elephant-king in the entry lives beside the lake.

channa.notes: The wanderer questions Ānanda in AN 3.71. DPD points to AN 3.72, whose visitor is an unnamed householder, and the entry’s citation lands at AN 5.180 (Gavesī). For the ill monk, MN 143 and SN 35.86 are adjacent to the actual accounts. DN 16 identifies Channa 03 by the order for the brahmadaṇḍa. In SN 22.90 Channa seeks instruction from Ānanda at Kosambī, but the text gives neither his former occupation nor the disciplinary episode. DPD assigns Thag 1.69 to the monk who died in MN 144, while Channa 03 claims the verse for the former charioteer. The verse names only Channa Thera. SN 35.93:4.2 mentions Channa solely in the chapter recap for SN 35.87.

ciravāsī.notes: The unplaced citation is identifiable at SN 42.11:2.18–22. Bhadraka names his boy and sends someone to check on him. The sutta says he lives away from home. The detail about school comes from the entry.

citta.notes: Thig 2.5:3.1 names Cittā Therī, a nun with a separate DPD sense. Both candidates here are men. The relevant passages in the grouped citations are AN 1.250 and AN 2.132. AN 1.258–267, AN 1.268–277 and AN 2.118–129 lack the householder. AN 6.59 concerns Dārukammika. Hatthisāriputta interrupts the elders in AN 6.60.

cittasena.notes: Both DN 20:10.9 and DN 32:10.8 call him gandhabba in the same sequence of names. DPD flags a commentarial tradition of two demigods. The recitations supply no distinguishing detail for a second individual.

cunda.notes: Cunda 02 explicitly covers both Mahācunda (MN 8:2.1) and Cunda the novice (MN 104:3.1). DPPN records conflicting traditions about their identity. DN 16 and Ud 8.5 each name the smith who gives the meal and the monk Cundaka who lays out the robe. The verses call the monk cundo at DN 16:4.41.11 and Ud 8.5:18.1, so a single identification would mislabel some taps. For Cunda 02, MN 117, MN 143, SN 46.17 and SN 47.12 are neighboring discourses. SN 35.79–81 miss the visit to Channa at SN 35.87. That visit takes place on Vulture’s Peak, while the Buddha is in the Bamboo Grove. SN 47.13 mentions Sāriputta’s bowl and robe. The relics and water-strainer are additional details in the entry.

cundī.notes: AN 5.32 names the princess and her brother. The other reference places her among laywomen in AN 8.91–117. AN 8.89 and 8.90 concern monastic discipline. AN 5.40:6.1 is a chapter recap.

cālikā.notes: AN 9.3 and Ud 4.1 give the town and mountain as the setting of Meghiya’s story. The page citation also catches AN 9.2, which gives no such setting.

cālā.notes: SN 5.6 and Thig 7.2 name the nun. SN 5.5 concerns Uppalavaṇṇā. Thag 1.42:1.1 is less clear. Revata addresses Cāle, a form DPD also links to the monk Cāla. Sujato gives Cālā, while the DPPN Revata entry takes the three addressees to be the sisters’ sons.

cātumā.notes: MN 67 opens at Cātumā in the myrobalan grove. The citation also catches MN 66, set at Āpaṇa.

cīrā.notes: SN 10.11 names the bhikkhunī Cīrā who receives a robe. The entry’s subject is the seven-year-old novice of the Twin Miracle story. DPPN calls their identity probable, and the sutta gives neither an age nor a miracle. A separate excerpt about the robe recipient could serve this sense. SN 10.10 concerns Sukkā and SN 10.12 concerns Āḷavaka.

cūlakokanadā.notes: SN 1.40 explicitly names Pajjunna’s younger daughter. She recites verses there, although the entry says she questioned the Buddha. SN 1.39 features the other Kokanadā.

dasama.notes: The visit of Dasama to Ānanda is in MN 52 and AN 11.16. The page references also catch MN 51 (Kandaraka) and AN 11.15 (the benefits of love).
